subject.title: Feature Request: Per-Agent Bedrock requestMetadata Injection for Multi-Agent Cost Attribution

question: Should OpenClaw's Amazon Bedrock provider add per-agent requestMetadata automatically, expose an opt-in/configured metadata path, or leave cost attribution to AWS-native profile/IAM patterns?
rationale: AWS records requestMetadata in invocation logs, warns against sensitive values, and says it is not a native Cost Explorer/CUR cost allocation tag, so this is a product and security policy choice before implementation. ([docs.aws.amazon.com](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/cost-mgmt-request-metadata.html))

options.title: Opt-in minimized Bedrock metadata
options.body: Add provider-owned support for sanitized, low-cardinality agent metadata or templates, document log-based attribution, and require redacted AWS proof.

options.title: Automatic per-agent metadata
options.body: Default-on injection maximizes coverage but intentionally sends local agent identity to AWS logs and needs explicit acceptance of that privacy tradeoff.

options.title: Document AWS-native attribution
options.body: Keep runtime unchanged and guide users toward application inference profiles, IAM principal attribution, Projects, or Workspaces for native billing attribution.

recommendation.title: Opt-in minimized Bedrock metadata
recommendation.body: Add provider-owned support for sanitized, low-cardinality agent metadata or templates, document log-based attribution, and require redacted AWS proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current extra-params and Bedrock pass-through history points to this provider/runtime seam as the likely decision area.
